doc_title: Campus LAN and Wireless LAN Solution Design Guide (CVD v2.0)
raw_text: A modular two-tier collapsed core design provides high availability, simplified routing, and deterministic convergence for small-to-medium enterprise campuses by combining core and distribution functions into a resilient Layer 3 switching platform.
extracted_principle: Two-tier Collapsed Core eliminates RoAS bottlenecks via centralized SVI routing

doc_title: Campus LAN and Wireless LAN Solution Design Guide (CVD v2.0)
chapter_section: Layer 2 Access Layer Design & Port Hardening
raw_text: Access layer switches should enforce edge security controls including PortFast and BPDU Guard on all host-facing ports to eliminate Spanning-Tree topology recalculations. Port Security with sticky MAC learning must be applied to bind unauthorized endpoint devices to physical access ports.
extracted_principle: Enforce PortFast, BPDU Guard, and Sticky MAC Port-Security on access interfaces

doc_title: Campus LAN and Wireless LAN Solution Design Guide (CVD v2.0)
raw_text: Uplinks from access switches to distribution/core switches should utilize IEEE 802.3ad Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) in active-active mode to prevent single points of failure and provide deterministic load sharing across bundled physical links.
extracted_principle: Dual-link LACP active EtherChannel for access-to-core uplinks

doc_title: Campus LAN and Wireless LAN Solution Design Guide (CVD v2.0)
raw_text: Rapid PVST+ (PVRST+) is recommended across all access and distribution VLANs to reduce failover convergence times below 2 seconds during link disruptions, maintaining explicit root bridge priorities for predictable traffic flow.
extracted_principle: Rapid-PVST+ deployment with deterministic Root Bridge priority configuration

doc_title: CVD: Small and Medium Enterprise Security & Segmentation Guide
raw_text: VLAN 1 must never be used for user or management traffic. A dedicated, unused Native VLAN (e.g., VLAN 999) should be assigned to 802.1Q trunks with no active SVIs to mitigate VLAN-hopping and double-tagging attack vectors.
extracted_principle: Quarantine default VLAN 1 and isolate Native VLAN 999 without SVI

doc_title: CVD: Small and Medium Enterprise Security & Segmentation Guide
raw_text: Extended Access Control Lists (ACLs) applied at ingress Layer 3 interfaces restrict lateral movement between user departments, isolating untrusted guest users and strictly filtering traffic to critical server farm services based on least-privilege protocols.
extracted_principle: Ingress Extended ACLs on SVIs to enforce lateral isolation and server access rules

doc_title: Enterprise Edge and Perimeter Firewall Design Guide
raw_text: The distribution/core layer forwards all external traffic via a dedicated point-to-point transit VLAN to a stateful perimeter firewall (Cisco ASA/NGFW) utilizing a floating default static route to isolate internal switching logic from perimeter NAT and WAN routing.
extracted_principle: Dedicated Transit VLAN (VLAN 70) and static default route to ASA Firewall

doc_title: Cisco SAFE Architecture: Zero Trust Workplace
chapter_section: DHCP Snooping and Rogue Gateway Defense
raw_text: DHCP Snooping must be globally enabled across all access switches, marking upstream trunk uplinks as trusted while untrusting access edge ports to prevent rogue DHCP server injections and man-in-the-middle attacks.
extracted_principle: DHCP Snooping with trusted uplinks and rate-limited access ports
